rows.claim: Perivascular influx ranks net parenchymal clearance tightly (Spearman rho >= 0.8) across the full plausible range of transport parameters.
rows.evidence: 2026-06-13_cc_data.json control_full_box: with Q, E, K independent log-uniform over 10^[-1,1] and the Peclet substrate held in [0.1,10], the Spearman correlation between influx (Q*C0) and net clearance (g*C_p) is only rho = 0.511 - well below the registered 0.80 acceptance bar.
rows.scope: synthetic steady-state series-conductance box, N=30000, seed=11; independent Q,E,K

rows.claim: No physiologically plausible single-mechanism bottleneck breaks the influx-to-clearance rank ordering.
rows.evidence: 2026-06-13_cc_data.json: a vascular-egress bottleneck (K log-uniform 10^[-2.5,-1.5]) gives rho = 0.038 and an interstitial-exchange bottleneck (E log-uniform 10^[-2.5,-1.5]) gives rho = 0.040 - both at or below the 0.30 reject line; the egress depth scan falls monotonically 0.511 -> 0.313 -> 0.171 -> 0.078 -> 0.022 as the egress band is depressed by 0 to 2.0 decades.
rows.scope: named single-mechanism bottleneck regimes on the same substrate, neutral Peclet preserved

rows.claim: When the imaged PVS conduit itself is the rate-limiting step, influx remains a near-perfect proxy for clearance.
rows.evidence: 2026-06-13_cc_data.json pvs_conduit_bottleneck: with E,K log-uniform 10^[1.5,2.5] so the series conductance g>>Q, the conduit is rate-limiting and the influx-clearance correlation is rho = 1.000 - the proxy holds exactly in this regime.
rows.scope: conduit-limited positive control; bounds the claim's validity to the regime where the imaged step is rate-limiting

rows.claim: In the living brain, perivascular tracer influx and net parenchymal clearance stay tightly coupled under a documented egress or exchange bottleneck (e.g. ageing, IIH, AQP4 loss).
rows.evidence: not tested - no in vivo tracer or imaging data were used; the true physiological ranges and covariances of Q, E and K are unknown, and covariation (e.g. Q and E rising together with pressure) could restore coupling. The decisive real-data discriminator was not run in this duel.
rows.scope: would require in vivo measurement of influx and net clearance under a documented bottleneck with real Q,E,K covariance; not run here
